trial_court: Family Court, Agartala, Title Suit(Divorce) No.150 of 2011
case_name: Shri Soumitra Ghosh vs Smt Shilpi Ghosh
facts_of_case: The parties solemnised their marriage in 2002. The appellant claimed the respondent had abnormal behaviour and was unwilling to co-habit. He sought a decree of divorce.

legal_principles.principle: A case of mental cruelty is established when a criminal case was filed by the respondent against her husband and his family members, and she has been living separately from the appellant for a long time.
legal_principles.held: Once it is shown that a criminal case was filed by the respondent against her husband and his family members and she has been living separately from the appellant for the last 15 long years, the inference is inevitable and the conclusion inescapable that there is no possibility of restoring normal conjugal life to the parties.
cited_cases: Dibyendu Das v. Nupur Deb (Das), (2014) 1 TLR 1018
Bhulu Rani Dey (Das) v. Rabi Dey, AIR 2012 Gauhati 128

legal_principles.principle: A party cannot take advantage of their own wrong.
legal_principles.held: She never did anything to humiliate the appellant, and he cannot take advantage of his own wrong.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's judgment refusing a decree of divorce was upheld.
